integration_decision.name: ARCHIVE_LOCK_IS_NOT_A_THREE_FILE_PUBLICATION_TRANSACTION
integration_decision.source_finding: ArchiveWriterLock in storage.py protects individual append_observations and load_observations calls, not the entire runner.run_once snapshot/compute/publish sequence. atomic_write_json uses per-file tempfile + os.replace; runner writes latest.json then audit_latest.json then anata_latest.json independently. Consequently a safe archive lock does not establish cross-file generation consistency. This is a source-level concurrency exposure, NOT an executed race reproduction.
integration_decision.improved_oracle: Use real no-network spawned processes and a child-A Event barrier immediately before A's anata_latest.json write. A reads empty archive; parent appends exactly one PIT-visible rowB; B reads 1/1 and publishes. For the existing unsynchronized implementation, B-completes-then-A-resumes should reveal cross-file disagreement if the suspected interleaving occurs; a future serialized implementation may block B until A is released. Parse all three files. Assert latest.coverage == audit.coverage == anata.quality.coverage, audit.visible_observation_count and audit.normalized_observation_count match the final generation (0 or 1), and anata.source_evidence contains rowB iff the final generation is B. Source-derived A/B expected ETF coverage 0 versus 1/3, subject to execution confirmation. Mixed generation => FAIL; barrier not reached, no A/B delta, missing provenance, or no cleanup => INVALID_TEST; deadlock => FAIL.
integration_decision.scope: Do not modify Specialist code; test contract only. The existing 112-line test remains a sequential preflight and violates compact Queue and finally cleanup requirements.
